text: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority from City Council to make a final decision. Transportation Services has reviewed the need for traffic calming (speed humps) on Woodville Avenue, between Pape Avenue and Broadview Avenue. The assessment indicates the warrant criteria as set out in the City of Toronto's Traffic Calming Policy has not been satisfied. Therefore, staff do not recommend the installation of speed humps on Woodville Avenue.

The Toronto and East York Community Council: 1. Waived the polling requirement under the City's Traffic Calming Policy and authorize the installation of traffic calming (speed humps) on Woodville Avenue; and a. authorized the installation of traffic calming (speed humps) on Woodville Avenue, between Pape Avenue and Broadview Avenue; and b. directed the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter sections of the roadway to install five speed humps on Woodville Avenue, between Pape Avenue and Broadview Avenue, for traffic calming purposes, generally as shown on Drawings Nos. TC-113 and TC-114, dated December 2022 and attached to the report (January 10, 2023) from the Director, Traffic Management, Transportation Services.
